audit.method: Read from the full term sheet by one AI reviewer, then checked against it twice by independent AI reviewers: first every line of the record against the document, then the document section by section against the record. Not signed off by a person. Every quote is looked up in the PDF text each time the tool runs.
audit.open_points:
The final record is at C:\Users\AFarid\Documents\Hackathon\key_credit_terms\data\audited\granite_construction_2025.json. The checker reports structure OK and 73 of 73 quotes exact. A diff against the first-audit record shows only the five fields listed in the changes differ; the header keys and the doc block are identical.

The walk from document to record (all 16 pages of the dump; page images 1-6, 10-12, 14 and 15) found no term missing from a row and no wrong figure. Every amount, percentage, ratio, date and day count in the record matches the page it is attributed to, including the amortisation table and the pricing level. Searches of the dump for Barclays, change of control, extension options, financial statements, budget, dividends, subordinated debt, mergers, cross default and judgments found nothing that would upgrade a not_stated or by_reference row.

First auditor's doubts, as resolved:
1. Covenant and information rows stay by_reference. The Covenants heading on page 10 covers the whole package and points to the Existing Credit Agreement, which is the style guide's open-list case.
2. fc_other stays by_reference. The financial covenants are introduced by 'including', and nothing closes the list.
3. mandatory_prepayment stays stated. The field guidance names currency fluctuation as an 'Other' event, and a not_stated row cannot carry the evidence for that line.
4. The $100m lien basket is now flagged in the printed line (see changes).
5. transferability is left as drafted, with restrictions on line 3. The consent terms need two lines, and moving the restrictions up would separate Borrower consent from deemed consent.
6. The 80% guarantor coverage assumption is now printed (see changes).
7. Default interest stays in the Events of Default row. It is labelled as default interest and the template has no pricing row.
8. doc.kind stays commitment_letter_term_sheet. The program's own rules engine gives that kind to any document whose first pages mention a commitment letter, as page 1 does.
9 and 10. The evidence gaps and soft-limit overruns are left as drafted. The unquoted sub-points were all confirmed on the pages the notes cite.

What the document itself cannot settle:
a. What the $100m limits in 'liens (i) permitting indebtedness in connection with permitted acquisitions not exceeding $100,000,000' (page 10): the indebtedness, the liens or the acquisition size.
b. Whether the Designated Borrowers count as 'non-guarantying subsidiaries' for the 20% cap (page 1).
c. The competitor contradiction on pages 10-11: a Borrower consent right for assignees in a similar line of business against an absolute ban on assignments to competitors. It is also unclear whether the Event of Default and existing-Lender exceptions reach similar-line-of-business assignees.
d. Whether the Interest Coverage and Leverage Ratio covenants are the only financial covenants.
e. Whether the Project Hub City acquisition itself triggers the 4.25x step-up, and the first covenant test date. The Closing Date is not given.

Not recorded because the template has no row for them: the pricing grid and fees (Addendum I), the Required Lenders threshold (more than 50%), and the Borrowers' right to reduce RCF commitments without penalty. The optional prepayment right is mentioned in the Mandatory Prepayment Events row.

doc.title: SUMMARY OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS - GRANITE CONSTRUCTION INCORPORATED - UP TO $1,100,000,000 SENIOR SECURED CREDIT FACILITY
doc.notes: Summary of Terms and Conditions (term sheet) for an up to $1.1bn senior secured credit facility (RCF + Term Loan) for Granite Construction Incorporated; it is the attachment to a commitment letter that is not part of the PDF, and it is undated. The terms are on pages 1-13 (label column on the left, text on the right) and pricing, fees and expenses are in Addendum I on pages 14-16. It is a new financing, expected to be documented as an amendment and restatement of the Existing Credit Agreement (Fourth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated June 2, 2022); there are no existing / proposed columns. Covenants, events of default and representations are 'substantially similar' to the Existing Credit Agreement and security is 'substantially identical' to the existing collateral, so most baskets, thresholds and reporting requirements are given by reference only; the commitment letter and fee letter (which define some capitalised terms and fees) are not included.

Sub-limits within the RCF: $150m standby letters of credit (performance and financial; financial L/Cs capped at $75m); $20m swingline loans (US dollars)
L/Cs available in US dollars and other readily available currencies to be determined, including Canadian dollars, sterling, yen, Mexican pesos and euros

evidence.quote: An up to $550,000,000 five-year revolving credit facility

facility.note: Total of $1.1bn is stated as 'an aggregate principal amount of up to $1,100,000,000' (page 2) and in the title (page 1). The RCF is 'up to' $550m; the Term Loan is a flat $550m. Facility size is before the incremental option (see Accordion). The L/C currencies are in the Multicurrency L/C Option section (page 2), which also caps L/Cs at the US dollar equivalent of $150m.

guarantor_coverage.note: The term sheet states the test as a cap on non-guarantor subsidiaries (20%, first line). The second line is derived: '>= 80%' is the arithmetic complement of that cap, not the term sheet's own words. It assumes the Designated Borrowers are not counted as 'non-guarantying subsidiaries': they are subsidiaries that are borrowers, jointly and severally liable, but the Guarantor definition carves them out ('other than a Designated Borrower', page 1, quoted under Guarantor(s)), and the term sheet does not say how the 20% cap treats them. Because the document cannot settle this, the assumption is printed in the line rather than left in this note. How often the test is measured is not stated. Material Subsidiary covers direct and indirect subsidiaries and is determined in accordance with GAAP.
